versions.changelog:
Version 1.2.0

- Expanded compatibility metadata (now includes Codex and orchestration details for Claude Code's ultracode).
- Added `paths: ["**/*.go"]` to explicitly specify processing scope for Go source files.
- Improved orchestration guidance and documentation on parallel sub-agents for code documentation and review.
- Documentation and reference files updated for clarity, precision, and up-to-date best practices.
- Removed deprecated file: `skill-card.md`.

- Clarified writing principles for documentation: added a dedicated section on concision, intent over paraphrase, anti-patterns, and preserving meaning.
- Expanded guidance on what to avoid in comments and documentation, emphasizing factual, user-focused writing and removal of boilerplate or marketing language.
- No changes to API or usage; updates are editorial and focused on strengthening the quality of generated documentation.
- Updated metadata version to 1.1.4.

golang-documentation 1.1.2

- Updated SKILL.md to clarify directory usage for architecture docs, minor formatting/clarity improvements, and corrected a small typo in the documentation checklist.
- Improved language in various documentation templates (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Refinements to library documentation guidance.
- Version bump in metadata.

- Version bump to 1.1.1 with updated metadata.
- Added an evals/evals.json file.
- Minor formatting and punctuation tweaks in the description and metadata.
- No changes to documentation content or usage instructions.

Initial release of golang-documentation skill:

- Provides comprehensive guidelines for documenting Go projects, covering godoc comments, README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, Go Playground demos, code examples, API docs, and llms.txt.
- Supports both write (generating/filling docs) and review (auditing/editing docs) modes, with parallel sub-agent suggestions.
- Includes detailed checklists, comment formatting standards, README section ordering, and cross-references to related skills.
- Applicable to Go libraries, applications/CLIs, and complex project architectures.
